question: What does a geometric-mean reporting comment require for comparison of individual monitoring-period values?

row.DMR_COMMENT_TEXT: TOTAL DISSOLVED SOLIDS (TDS) MEASURED AT OUTFALL 001.  REPORT THE GEOMETRIC MEAN VALUE OF THE WEEKLY VALUES.

judgment.semantic_question_used: Does the aggregated reporting requirement in the permit limit comment—report the geometric mean value of weekly values—apply to this BOD5 30-day average limit row (parameter 00310, 30 mg/L)?
judgment.interpretation: The DMR comment text reproduces permit footnote *6 language for Total Dissolved Solids discharge monitoring, but this occurrence is the BOD5 30-day average concentration limit (limit_value_id 3610673282, 30 mg/L, statistical base 3C/AVG). Authoritative permit text assigns geometric-mean-of-weekly-values reporting only to TDS discharge (*6), not to BOD5. BOD5 is limited and reported as a 30-day average at 30 mg/L with five samples per week per footnote *1 (sampling on at least five different days), consistent with secondary-treatment ELG requirements. The geometric-mean aggregated reporting obligation therefore does not govern this row despite the shared limit-set comment in structured ICIS data.
judgment.grounding: Structured row in sources/permit_limits.csv shows parameter 00310 (BOD) with DMR comment about TDS geometric mean attached at limit set 3600645646. documents/farmington/final_permit.txt Part I distinguishes BOD5 (30 mg/L 30-day avg, 5/Week *1) from TDS Discharge (*6, 1/Week, footnote *6 geometric mean of weekly values). documents/farmington/statement_of_basis.txt confirms BOD5 30 mg/L 30-day average limits and five-times-per-week BOD5/TSS monitoring.
